This is achieved by supporting training for undergraduate and graduate students and postdoctoral researchers through existing technical and skills-based training or certification programs and by providing for additional experiential learning experiences (SEC. 2(a)(1)(2)(A)(i)). Additionally, the Act mandates that merit review panels convened to evaluate proposals related to artificial intelligence systems research and related activities integrate perspectives from multiple and diverse research disciplines, including researchers from social science, technology ethics, normative ethics, legal, and linguistic disciplines (SEC. 2(a)(3)(g)).

policy_name: Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025 (Sec. 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership.")
question: What are the key objectives of the Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership Pilot Program?
answer_low_temp:
The key objectives of the Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership Pilot Program, as outlined in the provided context (SEC. 302), are as follows:

1. Establish a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies (SEC. 302(b)).
2. Incorporate the Pilot Program into an existing interagency coordinating group on wildfires (SEC. 302(c)(1)).
3. Identify key technology priority areas with respect to the deployment of wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies (SEC. 302(c)(2)).
4. Connect each covered entity selected to participate in the Pilot Program with the appropriate covered agency to coordinate real-time and on-the-ground testing of technology during wildland fire mitigation activities and training (SEC. 302(c)(3)).
5. Give priority to covered entities developing and applying emerging technologies that address issues identified by the Secretaries, including artificial intelligence, quantum sensing, computing and quantum-hybrid applications, augmented reality, and 5G private networks and device-to-device communications supporting nomadic mesh networks, for wildfire mitigation (SEC. 302(e)).
6. Make publicly available the key technology priority areas identified under subsection (c)(2) and invite covered entities to apply to test and demonstrate their technologies to address those priority areas (SEC. 302(f)).
7. Submit annual reports to the appropriate committees regarding the Pilot Program, including a list of participating covered entities, a brief description of the technologies tested, an estimate of the cost of acquiring the technology tested in the Pilot Program and applying it at scale, outreach efforts by Federal agencies to covered entities developing wildfire technologies, assessments of, and recommendations relating to, new technologies with potential adoption and application at-scale in the wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation efforts of Federal land management agencies (SEC. 302(g)).
8. The Pilot Program shall expire on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment of this Act (SEC. 302(h)).

Sources:
- Public Law 116-203, Sec. 30
answer_high_temp: 1) The Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership Pilot Program aims to establish a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies (Sec. 302(b)). 2) The program requires the Secretaries to identify key technology priority areas, including hazardous fuels reduction activities, dispatch communications, remote sensing and tracking, safety equipment, and common operating pictures or operational dashboards (Sec. 302(c)(2)). 3) The program prioritizes emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum sensing, computing and quantum-hybrid applications, augmented reality, and 5G private networks and device-to-device communications supporting nomadic mesh networks for wildfire mitigation (Sec. 302(e)). 4) The program requires the Secretaries to submit annual reports to the appropriate committees on the progress of the program, including a list of participating covered entities, descriptions of the technologies tested, cost estimates, outreach efforts, assessments of new technologies, and recommendations (Sec. 302(g)). 5) The program is set to expire 7 years after the date of enactment of this Act (Sec. 302(h)).
